create.name: Kunsang Yeshe Retreat Centre
create.bio:
Kunsang Yeshe Retreat Centre is a small Tibetan Buddhist centre in Katoomba, in the Blue Mountains west of Sydney, and part of the FPMT network begun by Lama Thubten Yeshe and Lama Zopa Rinpoche. Its name honours Kunsang Yeshe, the Lawudo Lama, a meditator of the Everest region whose rebirth Lama Zopa Rinpoche was recognised to be. Volunteers and a committee run the centre today, and its stated aim is to help people grow kinder, wiser and happier using Buddhist ideas, meditation and creativity.

Twice-weekly lunchtime sits in the gompa are open to anyone without booking, and a monthly Medicine Buddha session invites people to dedicate the practice to friends, family or animals who are unwell or have died. Local students lead introductory courses on Buddhism, while visiting FPMT geshes and nuns give weekend teachings and online series, several of them recorded and shared through its audio-visual library and YouTube channel. Members receive discounts and library borrowing, and the centre hopes one day to add a residential retreat property.

courses.title: Drop-in Meditation
courses.description: A short guided sit in the Katoomba gompa at lunchtime on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Nobody needs to book, and newcomers are welcome.

courses.title: Medicine Buddha Healing Meditation
courses.description: A monthly Friday lunchtime practice of the Medicine Buddha, where those present can name people or animals who are unwell or have passed away for the dedication prayers.

courses.title: Become a Member
courses.description: Annual membership that helps keep the centre running and brings reduced programme fees, use of the library and a vote at the yearly meeting. Half-year and concession rates are offered.
courses.price: Single: $130; Single Concession: $100; Family: $190; Family Concession: $160 (full year)

free_resources.title: Audio-Visual Resources
free_resources.description: Recordings of past teaching series at the centre, including the Heart Sutra, Buddhist views on death and dying, and lojong mind training, offered freely with donations invited.
